messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert: HIGH_LATENCY detected for dedicated tenant 'quantumhealth' on reserved-pool q2. p95 generation latency > 2.5s for the last 5m. Alert id: PD-98321

pagerduty: page fired -> oncall: Alyssa

Alyssa (oncall): acked. pulling graphs now. 

Alyssa (oncall): Raja, can you grab KV cache / scheduling dashboards? seeing p95 and some 503 spikes in the last 2m.

Raja (sre): on it. hitting the metrics now. looks like IO wait on pool q2 hosts, disk iops spiking on node set a3-a5.

Clara (platform): I see scheduled maintenance jobs overlap with burst windows, and autoscaler didn't trigger because headroom was low. Noted several preemption events.

Jess (support): Heads-up — QuantumHealth's app team just pinged support. They see timeouts in prod for a subset of requests (~3% traffic).

Alyssa (oncall): Impact estimate? Jess, ask them if they see user-facing errors or background job failures.

Jess (support): sent message to customer rep: "We're investigating elevated latencies and intermittent timeouts, working on mitigation now."

Raja (sre): quick triage: KV cache hit-rate unchanged. latency correlates with storage throughput saturation on dedicated hosts. temporary mitigation options: 1) route some tenant traffic to fallback reserved pool in us-west-2, 2) throttle low-priority routes for QuantumHealth, 3) add burst nodes (if capacity available).

Clara (platform): I can trigger burst-add, but need approval — it may violate reserved commit if we oversubscribe. If we do a controlled burst, we should set a 30m window and alert billing.

Tom (devex): We have a previously tested route hack to fall back to a smaller model variant for non-critical paths. Patch ready: curl to promote route fallback: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.internal/routes/fallback \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TKN" \
  -d '{"tenant":"quantumhealth","routes":[{"path":"/v1/generate","priority":"low","model":"q2-small","timeout":12000}] }'
```

Alyssa (oncall): Good. Plan: 1) enable model fallback for low-priority routes (Tom) 2) apply temporary throttling for background/low-priority jobs (Raja) 3) Clara to attempt 10% burst-add if we still see >2s p95 after steps 1-2. I'll be primary owner.

Tom (devex): I flipped route fallback flag at 3542110102. Monitoring logs for error rate.

Raja (sre): applying soft throttle on background queues now. command: 
```
rbctl throttle set --tenant quantumhealth --queue background --rate 50r/s --window 600s
```
applied at 3542110188.

incident-bot: Note: runbook step executed: MODEL_FALLBACK_TRIGGERED by Tom at 3542110102

Clara (platform): starting 2 burst nodes (10% capacity) at 3542110220. estimated ready in 90s.

Alyssa (oncall): p95 dropping — current telemetry: p95 ~1.8s, error rate down to 1.2%. Great. Keep watching for 10m.

Jess (support): Customer updated: "Thanks for quick response, seeing improvement on our side"

Raja (sre): keeping throttle and fallback for now. will unwind throttles after 30m if stable.

Clara (platform): burst nodes came up at 3542110340. no further IO saturation on pool hosts.

Tom (devex): Confirmed fallback acceptance logs: 2.1% requests routed to q2-small with successful responses.

Alyssa (oncall): OK moving to monitor->stabilize. I'll handoff to Raja for 1hr post-incident watch. If any regression, repage.

Alyssa (oncall): incident summary (for postmortem): "Reservoir of scheduled maintenance + low autoscaler headroom caused temporary IO saturation on QuantumHealth dedicated pool. Mitigations: model fallback, soft throttling of low-priority queues, 10% burst-add. Impact: ~3% requests saw higher latency/timeouts, customer reported improvement after mitigations. Next steps: schedule autoscaler tuning, avoid maintenance during tenant peak windows, add runbook snippet for negotiated burst-add approvals."

Raja (sre): taking on-watch. I'll create an incident ticket PD-98321-IO and assign postmortem owner.

incident-bot: PagerDuty note: incident acknowledged by Alyssa at 3542109888, escalated to Raja (oncall) at 3542110400.

Alyssa (oncall): handing off to Raja — leaving channel but reachable. :wave:

Raja (sre): ack. I'll update the thread and close when stable for 60m.

Jess (support): I'll follow up with QuantumHealth PM with the summary and ETA for postmortem.

Clara (platform): tagging billing for burst oversubscribe: @billing-team please standby for short burst-add on tenant quantumhealth.

Tom (devex): adding logs and commands used into the incident doc at https://redwood.internal/incidents/PD-98321

Raja (sre): closing loop: last check at 3542110448, p95 1.7s, error rate 0.7%. marking incident stabilizing.

incident-bot: Incident thread locked for edits at 3542110450 by Raja.
